''Pío Pío'' | founded = {{start date and age|1949|8|22|df=yes}} | stadium = [[Estadio Gran Canaria]] | capacity = 32,400{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/en/club/gran-canaria-stadium|title=Gran Canaria Stadium|publisher=UD Las Palmas|access-date=16 January 2020|archive-date=14 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014003359/https://www.udlaspalmas.es/en/club/gran-canaria-stadium|url-status=dead}} | chairman = Miguel Ángel Ramírez | chrtitle = President | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Rubén de la Barrera]] | league = {{Spanish football updater|Las Palmas}} | season = {{Spanish football updater|Las Palmas2}} | position = {{Spanish football updater|Las Palmas3}} | website = {{URL|https://www.udlaspalmas.es/|udlaspalmas.es}} | pattern_la1 = _laspalmas2627h | pattern_b1 = _laspalmas2627h | pattern_ra1 = _laspalmas2627h | pattern_sh1 = _laspalmas2627h | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFF00 | body1 = FFFF00 | rightarm1 = FFFF00 | shorts1 = 0000FF | socks1 = 0000FF | pattern_la2 = _laspalmas2627a | pattern_b2 = _laspalmas2627a | pattern_ra2 = _laspalmas2627a | pattern_sh2 = _laspalmas2627a | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = 0000FF | body2 = 0000FF | rightarm2 = 0000FF | shorts2 = FFFF00 | socks2 = FFFF00 |pattern_la3 = _laspalmas2627t |pattern_b3 = _laspalmas2627t |pattern_ra3 = _laspalmas2627t |pattern_sh3 = _laspalmas2627t |pattern_so3 = |leftarm3 = ffffff |body3 = ffffff |rightarm3 = ffffff |shorts3 = ffffff |socks3 = ffffff | current = 2026–27 UD Las Palmas season }} '''Unión Deportiva Las Palmas, S.A.D.'''[http://www.udlaspalmas.es/club-historia-identidad Historia – Nombre del club (History – Club name)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121118082542/http://www.udlaspalmas.es/club-historia-identidad |date=18 November 2012 }}; Las Palmas' official website {{in lang|es}} is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Las Palmas de Gran Canaria]], [[Canary Islands]], Spain. The club currently compete in [[Segunda División]], the 2nd tier of the [[Spanish football league system]] following their relegation from [[La Liga]] in the [[2024–25 La Liga|2024–25 season]]. Nicknamed ''Los Amarillos'', the club was founded on 22 August 1949 as a result of a merger between five clubs in the Canary region. The club initially played in the [[Estadio Insular]] before beginning hosting their home matches at the [[Estadio Gran Canaria]] in 2003. Las Palmas have been [[Segunda División]] champions four times, in [[1953–54 Segunda División|1953–54]], [[1953–54 Segunda División|1963–64]], [[1984–85 Segunda División|1984–85]] and [[1999–2000 Segunda División|1999–2000]], and have won the [[Segunda División B]] twice, in [[1992–93 Segunda División B|1992–93]] and [[1995–96 Segunda División B|1995–96]]. They have been runners-up in [[La Liga]] once, in [[1968–69 La Liga|1968–69]], and runners-up in the [[Copa del Rey]], in [[1977–78 Copa del Rey|1977–78]]. Las Palmas is the only side in Spanish football to achieve back-to-back promotions to La Liga in their first two seasons. They had a 19-year run in the competition, ending in [[1982–83 La Liga|1982–83]] and has been promoted to La Liga on four additional occasions since that time, achieving it recently in [[2022–23 La Liga|2022–23]]. Since its foundation, the club has played with yellow and blue as their primary and secondary colours. They have a fierce rivalry with [[Tenerife|neighbouring island]] [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]], with whom they contest the [[Canary Islands derby]]. The two clubs are among the most isolated professional football clubs in Europe since they play their away games on the distant Spanish mainland."}}
